note: Hand-written search shorthand that no registry ID segment or wiki display name spells out on its own. Every entry here is community shorthand the maintainer is genuinely confident is unambiguous mid-match -- a wrong alias sends a player to the wrong page mid-match, which is worse than a missing one, so this file stays conservative and small on purpose. Add an entry only when the shorthand is widely used, has exactly one sensible target, and is not already produced by pipeline.normalize.aliases.generate_aliases (a whole-phrase or a plain underscore-segment of the entity's own registry ID needs no curated entry). See pipeline/normalize/curated.py for the loader and pipeline/normalize/aliases.py for how a curated alias is weighted against a generated one. One entry was rejected once and is now accepted, and both halves are worth recording. `fort` looked obvious for Fortune and was refused, because this tool is built for draftout matches and in that setting `fort` means the Nether Fortress far more often than it means the enchantment; the refusal noted that structures were not enumerated yet and that the question would need answering the moment Phase 6c landed. It has landed, `minecraft:fortress` is a real entity, and `fort` now points at it rather than at the enchantment it never meant. `dungeon` points at the Monster Spawner rather than at a structure of its own on purpose: a dungeon is a feature, not a `worldgen/structure` member, so it has no page, and the spawner is the block a player is actually looking for when they type it. `jungle temple` is the name the game's own loot table uses (`chests/jungle_temple`) for the structure the registry calls `jungle_pyramid`, so both names reach the one page.
